answer: Copying a key is free, so software alone cannot stop sybils. The fix is hardware-rooted attestation: each agent generates its signing key inside a secure enclave tied to one physical die and publishes a fresh quote every epoch. A clone cannot export that key, so a thousand fake personas cost a thousand chips. The ledger counts the enclave serial as the identity unit. An expired quote is a relic carrying no weight, so a dormant farm cannot revive a stored atlas of keys. Influence accrues only to enclaves still proving liveness, making the zenith of reputation a slow climb, not a purchase.
